newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CS FIRST BOSTON MAINTAINS 'BUY' ON PICK.
newsitem.headline: CS FIRST BOSTON MAINTAINS 'BUY' ON PICK.

text.p: CS First Boston said it maintained a 'buy' recommendation on shares in Hungarian meat processor Pick Szeged Rt, saying the company's first half figures met its expectations.
"Pick's sales grew by 15.2 percent, while margins remained roughly unchanged - in line with our expectations," CSFB's analyst Pal Bogar said in a company report.
Pick released its first half results on Monday and said its sales and profits were above its plans.
Pick's consolidated pre-tax profit in the first half of 1997 was 1.19 billion forints compared with 901 million forints in the same period of 1996 and a plan of 1.12 billion forints.

Bogar added that a possible acquisition of meat processor Ringa Rt, one of the largest meat processing companies in Hungary with a 10 to 12 percent market share, would bring a major enhancement in Pick's value.

"We believe that Ringa is a good fit for Pick operationally...," he said. "The deal also fits into Pick's acquisition strategy taking advantage of the consolidation trends in the Hungarian meat processing industry."
CSFB expected Pick to continue its stable growth in the future supported by its acquisition strategy, favourable macro trends in Hungary and the gradual EU integration.
